correctness.rationale: For all rim lengths n>=4 the map is a product of involutory binary local shears, hence an automorphism. Inspecting RESULT.md and checks/verify.py at the returned exact blob paths confirms (I+L)y=(I+U)x, the polynomial determinant det((z+1)I+zL+U), the interior geometric-sum recurrence and the four-residue 3-by-3 determinant. Nonunit-eigenvalue eigenspaces have dimension at most one; at eigenvalue one the exceptional three chains occur exactly for 4|n, with lengths (1,1,1) if 8|n and (3,1,1) if n≡4 (mod8). Therefore cyclic invariant factor P_n when 4∤n, and two (z+1) summands plus P_n/(z+1)^2 when 4|n. On each cyclic binary module ker(F^d-I) has dimension deg gcd(R,z^d+1), with two additional dimensions when 4|n; Möbius inversion gives primitive cycles for EVERY d. The reciprocal polynomial has correct n=4 empty-sum boundary; all states are periodic due to invertibility. Independently constructed sweep and GF(2) charpoly computations for n=4..16 matched the stated formula and eigenvalue-one nullities [3,0,1,0,3,0,1,0,3,0,1,0,3]. The exact package checks further test n<=80 but are finite, not substitutes for algebraic general proof.

value.rationale: The fixed hub-first sweep is a natural asynchronous extension of binary Rule 150 from a ring to its wheel join. Its all-size exact four-residue transition in minimal number of F2[z] module generators (1 vs 3) is a structural Jordan phenomenon, not a small finite experiment. The characteristic polynomial and invariant-factor decomposition compute every temporal period population without period cutoff, and the five/eight-rim examples illustrate genuinely different dynamical regimes. These are motivated reusable invariants of ordered graph parity dynamics, beyond elementary general facts about shears.

limitations: Only hub-first rim-contiguous ordering over F2 and n>=4; no general arbitrary order, nonlinear local rule or characteristic q result. External scholarly originality is qualified.
